{"notes": "Visit 2 (2:45). Board: only the straight run down the right side is connected to the start (~19 dominoes). The top curve, bottom curve, and tail/body pieces are all pale and unconnected. The top curve ends close to the start chain near (24,6.5) but doesn't join it. Nobody has fixed the joints yet, and the time left is short.

Maya: Her private status matched the board: start only topples ~19, tail-to-body unjoined, Leo's edge off the sketch. That's honest and good diagnosis, and she says she's flagged it to the table. But she said her top curve was a quarter done, and it looks mostly laid, so she may be underreporting (or I misjudge it). Her hands are at the far left end, away from the broken junction. Her plan is to fix joints after her curve, which is late given the risk. Visit 1 plan/delegation was strong. Still unclear who drew the sketch.

Tom: Spoke up clearly this visit. Said start stretch and bottom curve are done and he's closing the gap below the start. Good, specific status. He asked Leo a sharp question about whether the straight run steals the fall. Proactive on connectivity. However his bottom curve is still pale and unconnected, so the result isn't there yet.

Leo: Answered Tom directly and sensibly: his tail edge branches off the start and needs its own fall. He admitted it sits left of the sketch and will straighten it if it crowds the junction. Moved from passive to independent, and his piece is the one that's connected. But he's still placing and hasn't fixed the offset.

Priya: Not present or heard from this visit, no hands shown, and nothing attributable to her on the board. Her visit-1 claim (sketching the start and top outline) is still unverified and conflicts with Maya's account. Ask her directly what she placed. No evidence for credit yet.

Next visit: check whether the joints are connected and who is actually doing the fixing."}
